title: What Actually Is a VPN?
sources: Privacy Guides, 'VPN Overview' (privacyguides.org/en/basics/vpn-overview): VPNs encrypt traffic between your device and the VPN provider's server; without one your ISP can see the domains you request, with one it only sees that you are connected to a VPN; a VPN hides your IP from websites; it shifts the trust you place in your network to the VPN server, and the provider can see and modify your traffic the same way your ISP could; a VPN does not give absolute anonymity

EBSCO Research Starters, 'Virtual Private Network (VPN)': Microsoft software engineer Gurdeep Singh Pall coauthored the first VPN protocol, PPTP, in 1996, so coworkers could work securely from home or remote locations

SmarterMSP, 'Tech Time Warp: a look back at the first VPN': Microsoft employees including Singh-Pall developed PPTP (with U.S. Robotics); 'It really allowed people to work effectively and securely from home.'

lines.text: Everything you do online goes through your Wi-Fi,
and your internet provider, who can see every site you visit.
lines.caps: AND YOUR *INTERNET | *PROVIDER | WHO CAN *SEE | EVERY *SITE | YOU *VISIT

lines.text: A VPN wraps it all in a scrambled, locked tunnel,
lines.caps: A VPN *WRAPS | IT *ALL | IN A *SCRAMBLED | LOCKED *TUNNEL

lines.text: straight to a VPN server somewhere else.
Now your provider just sees gibberish,
and websites see the server's address, not yours.
That's handy on sketchy coffee shop Wi-Fi.
The first VPN came from Microsoft in nineteen ninety-six,
so people could work safely from home.
the VPN company now sees what your provider used to,
lines.caps: THE VPN *COMPANY | NOW *SEES | WHAT YOUR *PROVIDER | *USED TO

lines.text: A VPN doesn't hide you, it just changes who's watching.
lines.caps: A VPN *DOESN'T | *HIDE YOU | IT JUST *CHANGES | WHO'S *WATCHING
